# Casberi

> Keep it moving, privately. Your life and money are spread across accounts; you spend the day switching between apps to get anything done. Casberi is a wallet that keeps it all moving, privately: keep up with your feeds and finances in one place. Free on iPhone and iPad, with no Casberi account, and read on your device.

Key facts:

- Free on the App Store for iPhone and iPad.
- More than 100 apps connect, among them Gmail, iCloud Mail, Calendar, Reminders, Photos, Apple Health, Apple Wallet, GitHub, GitLab, Linear, Jira, Notion, Slack, Trello, Stripe, Vercel, Cloudflare, AWS, App Store Connect, Readwise, RSS, Substack, YouTube, Spotify, Bluesky, X, Instagram, Threads, TikTok, Telegram, Claude, ChatGPT, Claude Code and Gemini.
- One page: Home starts with your money (the balance, Public by network, Private by place, then Account, Risks and Apps), and under it what is new: Needs you, Activity and a section for each kind of app. Move, the circle at the bottom and the only thing on the bar, is what you do with your money. A swipe right goes back. On iPad, Home is cards and Activity a place of its own.
- Activity: on iPhone the lower half of Home. Your apps' icons, then what needs you, then your watchlist, Spending and latest move, then a section for each kind of app — Day, Notes, Social, Work, Media, Life and Agents — with one row per app: its icon and its newest thing.
- Home: one balance across self-custody accounts (Ethereum, Base, Arbitrum, Optimism, Polygon, World Chain, HyperEVM, Monad, Robinhood Chain, Tempo, Solana and Bitcoin), Coinbase, Kraken, Binance and Gemini, ETH validators, and Wise and Apple Wallet cash. It leads with the balance and its day, Public as a row per network and Private as a row per place (Privacy Pools, Railgun, Aztec); tap the balance for Holdings. Risks counts what is new.
- Move: an account of your own in three parts — a public account (a Safe on Base, Ethereum and Robinhood Chain, no seed phrase), a private balance (0xBow Privacy Pools and Railgun on Ethereum: you pick for ETH and USDC, any other token goes to Railgun) and a private account (Aztec, for private apps and payments, proved on the iPhone) — and five verbs, each held to approve and signed with Face ID: Buy (tokens by card through Stripe, or a gift card from Bitrefill), Earn (on Aave), Receive, Send and Swap (now, at a price through CoW Swap, or Sweep: every token under $1 or $5 on a network into ETH). Send pays a contact, a name or a zk.money tag, from your public account or privately. Swaps go straight to Uniswap and Aerodrome from the phone, through Tor; a swap to another network goes through Across; a private swap stays inside Railgun. On Base, a send short of ETH pays its fee in USDC. Every buy, send and swap can round up to the next $1 or $5: the change earns on Aave and moves into the private balance at $10.
- Apps: under the balance on Home, with a search field over every app you have, by category. Contacts (in Social) is everyone you deal with, with Send for a contact who has a wallet and Pay for one with a zk.money tag. Calendar (in Day) opens its own page. The Wallet folder holds the Aztec apps you have connected.
- Subscriptions are found on their own from your cards, Apple Wallet and Rocket Money; what they cost lives in Spending.
- Agents: read what the agents you use did, in one place. Ask Claude, ChatGPT, Gemini and others with your own key, kept in the Keychain and sent from the device straight to that provider; your own OpenAI-compatible server; or Apple Intelligence with no key.
- Notes and voice notes, Contacts across your accounts, and share cards. Widgets for your notes, your wallet, your feed and your watchlist.
- No Casberi account, no server, no analytics. Every request that names a wallet goes through Tor on iPhone and iPad. iCloud sync is opt-in. Export, import and delete-everything are real controls.

## Docs

- [Docs](https://casberi.app/docs.html): why Casberi exists, the problems it answers, and a walkthrough of every surface
- [Privacy](https://casberi.app/privacy.html): what is stored, where, and what Casberi never does

## How it's built

- [Source](https://github.com/alexanderchopan/casberi): the whole app, public under the GPLv3
- [Architecture and threat model](https://github.com/alexanderchopan/casberi/blob/main/docs/architecture.md): what the app holds, what signs, what leaves the device, what it trusts
- [Every host](https://github.com/alexanderchopan/casberi/blob/main/docs/hosts.md): every host the app can reach, generated from the code
- [Verify it yourself](https://github.com/alexanderchopan/casberi/blob/main/docs/verify-it-yourself.md): one command per claim, with the output to expect
- [Dependencies](https://github.com/alexanderchopan/casberi/blob/main/docs/dependencies.md): version, source and licence of each
- [Security policy](https://github.com/alexanderchopan/casberi/blob/main/SECURITY.md): how to report a vulnerability
